title: A Housing-Centric Framework for Estimating Urban Quality of Life Using Objective Data
institution: Virginia Tech, Dept. of Computer Science (Alexandria)
region: Washington D.C. Metropolitan Area (DC, VA: Arlington/Fairfax/Loudoun + Alexandria/Fairfax/Falls Church; MD: Montgomery/Prince George’s)
summary: Paper proposes a rental-housing–centric Quality of Life (QoL) index that integrates objective indicators: rental prices, transit accessibility, air quality, walkability, and green space proximity/density. Two-round HDBSCAN clusters housing units for AQI assignment; PCA derives indicator weights; a PostGIS-backed system plus FastAPI/React app exposes scores at listing level.

title: Composite QoL Index
explanation: QoL for housing unit h_i is the weighted sum of normalized indicator values x_{ij}. Weights w_j are derived from PCA component loadings (PC1-based).
indicators: Number of bus stops within 1 mile
Number of green spaces within 1 mile

definitions.name: AQI
definitions.desc: Air quality composite from pollutant concentrations. Higher raw AQI = worse air.

definitions.name: Nearest Bus Stop (mi)
definitions.desc: Euclidean distance from listing to closest WMATA bus stop.

definitions.name: # Bus Stops (<=1 mi)
definitions.desc: Count of distinct bus stops within a 1-mile radius of the listing.

definitions.name: Nearest Green Space (mi)
definitions.desc: Euclidean distance from listing to boundary of nearest OSM green space.

definitions.name: # Green Spaces (<=1 mi)
definitions.desc: Count of distinct green spaces within a 1-mile radius.

notes: Right-skew evident in price, distance-to-bus, #bus stops, distance-to-green-space.
High correlation observed between distance-to-green and distance-to-bus (urban planning co-location).
Mitigate outliers with distance capping; PCA later handles multicollinearity.

section: AQI Spatial Assignment via Two-Round HDBSCAN
steps: Round 1: HDBSCAN finds dense neighborhood clusters; noise marked for pass 2.
Round 2: Relaxed parameters to capture sparser suburban clusters; remaining noise snapped to nearest cluster.
Per-cluster centroid computed; AQI fetched at centroid; all cluster members inherit AQI.
why: AQI monitors are sparse; clustering smooths spatial noise and avoids missing/irrelevant sensors.
evaluation: Parameter grid search; select by silhouette, cluster count, and noise fraction.

transformations: Log transform: price; distances; counts (where skewed).
Z-score standardization on all indicators before PCA.
Direction alignment: invert features where higher is worse (AQI, distance to bus, distance to green). Rental price left ambiguous; direction learned by PCA.

interpretation: PC1 (~47%) captures dominant pattern across price, air quality, and proximity/density metrics. Literature supports using PC1 as composite when >40% variance explained.

note: All features standardized; direction inverted where higher raw values imply worse QoL.

guidelines: Compute standardized indicator vector for a listing; apply PC1-derived weights for QoL.
For new areas, rebuild HDBSCAN clusters and re-fetch AQI per cluster centroid.
Update weights via PCA when adding/removing indicators to maintain objectivity.
Expose listing-level QoL via API and cache map tiles for responsive UX.

q: Which indicators are included in the composite QoL?
a: Price, AQI (inverted), EPA Walkability Index, distance to nearest bus stop (inverted), number of bus stops within 1 mile, distance to nearest green space (inverted), number of green spaces within 1 mile.
Run PCA on standardized indicators and use normalized absolute loadings from PC1 as weights (PC1 ≈ 47% variance).

q: Why use two-round HDBSCAN for AQI?
a: AQI monitors are spatially sparse. Clustering creates coherent geographies; centroid AQI is assigned to all cluster members, reducing missing or misleading values.
AQI and distances (to bus stop, to green space). Rental price is ambiguous and left for PCA to resolve.

q: What are the approximate normalized weights?
a: Nearest green space (0.201), nearest bus stop (0.199), # bus stops (0.194), # green spaces (0.141), AQI (0.123), Walkability (0.120), Price (0.023).
DC; VA (Arlington, Fairfax, Loudoun + Alexandria/Fairfax/Falls Church); MD (Montgomery, Prince George’s).

q: How to extend to new regions?
a: Swap data sources of same semantics (transit, price, AQI, walkability, green spaces), rebuild clusters, recompute PCA weights, and regenerate QoL.

entries.definition: Quality of Life; composite measure of livability across objective indicators.
Hierarchical Density-Based Spatial Clustering; finds dense spatial clusters and handles noise.
Principal Component Analysis; transforms correlated indicators into orthogonal components and supports weight derivation.
National Walkability Index; 1–20 scale of pedestrian friendliness at block-group level.
Air Quality Index; higher raw AQI means worse air quality; inverted for QoL contribution.
Spatial extension for PostgreSQL enabling geometry types and spatial indices/queries.
